meta.note: Hand-written findings about data/payroll.json (which is generated by scripts/build-payroll-dataset.mjs from the original county ZIP). Every figure cited in citedFigures is machine-checked against data/payroll.json by `npm run data:audit`; the prose around it is editorial and must be reviewed by a person. Promotion of any status to a stronger one is a human decision.
meta.terminology: OFFICIAL PAYROLL AMOUNT means a figure printed in the county's payroll export. COMPARISON FIGURE means a number this project calculated for context. A difference between them is a research question, not a conclusion, and is never characterized beyond what the records establish.

keyObservations.title: BCC employees only
keyObservations.text: The county stated it can provide information for the Board of County Commissioners and not the constitutional offices. Nothing here describes the Sheriff's Office, Clerk, Tax Collector, Property Appraiser, Supervisor of Elections, School Board, or municipal/utility employers, and none of them are mixed in.

keyObservations.title: Rate and wages paid are different measurements
keyObservations.text: "Fiscal Non-OT YTD Wages" is one combined amount paid in the period. It is not a salary rate, and the county's report does not split it into base pay, leave payout, special or acting pay, or allowances. Overtime is reported separately. The census gives a current annualized base rate, which is a rate and not money paid. Employer-paid benefits and employer taxes are county costs, not employee pay.

keyObservations.title: Earlier salary figures and county wages paid may measure different things
keyObservations.text: An older "salary" figure can be an annualized rate at a particular point in time; the county's payroll export reports wages paid over a defined period. They are not automatically the same measurement, and a difference between them does not by itself show that either is wrong. For all five people in the earlier salary leads, the county's current annualized base rate divided by the earlier figure is 1.0300 (within about $0.11), and the two payroll reports show wages per pay period rising about 3.0% between fiscal years for the County Manager, the two Assistant County Managers employed in both periods, the Fire Chief, and the Fire Marshal. That is consistent with the earlier figures having been annualized rates before a 3% adjustment. The census supplies only the current rate, so a prior rate cannot be confirmed from this response.
keyObservations.doesNotEstablish: What the earlier figures actually measured, where they came from, or that the adjustment was exactly 3%. No supplied county record states any of these.

keyObservations.title: Commissioner official payroll amounts and a comparison figure
keyObservations.text: OFFICIAL PAYROLL AMOUNT: the county's payroll export shows the non-OT wages paid to each commissioner. COMPARISON FIGURE: this project's calculation of the Charter salary of $37,000 ÷ 26 bi-weekly periods ($1,423.08) × the number of pay periods in the report. For FY2025-26 through September 16, 2026 (25 pay periods, comparison figure $35,577.00), the official payroll amounts for Kristen Burke and Alexandra Compere equal the comparison figure. The official payroll amounts for Elizabeth Condon, James Renninger and John Sgromolo are $525.00, $2,897.00 and $1,259.75 above it. For FY2024-25 (26 pay periods, comparison figure $37,000.08) Burke and Compere again equal the comparison figure, and Condon and Renninger are $1,275.00 and $2,865.88 above it; partial-period figures for Cella and Sgromolo are not compared. The research question is: what accounts for the difference between the comparison compensation figure and the wages reported in the county payroll export?
keyObservations.doesNotEstablish: Why any amount differs, whether the comparison figure is the right benchmark, or that any amount is anything other than what the county's payroll recorded. The records give no explanation and none is offered here.
checksPerformed: The five differences were recomputed independently from the original ZIP; none is a whole number of pay periods (0.37, 0.89, 0.90, 2.01, 2.04), so an extra, missing, or shifted pay period does not produce them.

Condon, Renninger and Sgromolo are full-period employees in FY2025-26 (hired before October 1, 2025, no termination date), so a partial period does not apply. Sgromolo (hired 2024-11-19) and Cella (ended 2024-11-18) are excluded from the FY2024-25 comparison.
The 25 pay periods for FY2025-26 are supported independently of the commissioners: 62 of 80 salaried non-commissioner peers fit 25 periods within 2%, against 3, 10 and 3 for 24, 26 and 27.
limitations: The comparison figure depends on the $37,000 Charter salary as recorded in this project's source register (an official county agenda attachment reproducing the Charter provision). The Charter text itself could not be re-read in this pass, because the county website refused automated access, so the comparison is not presented as definitive.
The FY2024-25 count of 26 pay periods is inferred (from the commissioners' own pattern and the length of the period) and has no independent census-rate check.
It is assumed all commissioners share one pay calendar; the files cannot confirm that. Using the unrounded $37,000 × N ÷ 26 changes every difference by $0.08.

keyObservations.title: Names differ between files; identities are linked by hire date and position
keyObservations.text: The payroll reports use preferred first names and the census uses legal names, and neither file carries an employee ID. Records were linked on last name + hire date (+ position where needed). The census lists two different employees with the legal name William Latham: the Assistant County Manager hired 2020-11-23 (listed in payroll as "Latham, Charlie") and an unrelated employee in a non-executive position with a different hire date and a different payroll name. They are different people and must never be merged; the second is not named here because they are outside the named group. The build stops if two payroll workers ever resolve to the same census record.

keyObservations.title: The census "Years in Current Position" field is unreliable
keyObservations.text: For more than a third of active employees this field disagrees with the census's own effective date. It is not used for any published figure and should not be used to state anyone's time in a position.

leadChecks.identityAndTitle: Confirmed by official records: payroll and census both list Howard Wanamaker as County Manager, hired 2019-06-18.
leadChecks.finding: OFFICIAL PAYROLL AMOUNTS: the county's export reports non-OT wages of $262,071.70 (plus $991.28 overtime) for FY2024-25 and $259,474.64 for FY2025-26 through September 16, 2026. The census lists a current annualized base rate of $247,654.32, which equals 1.0300 × the earlier $240,441 figure, so the earlier figure may have been an annualized rate at an earlier point in time; that is not confirmed. COMPARISON FIGURE: the current annualized rate × 25 ÷ 26 is $238,129.15, and the reported FY2025-26 wages are $21,345.49 above it. The research question is: what payroll components account for the difference between the current annualized-rate comparison and reported wages during the period? Among 80 salaried peers, 62 are within 2% of the same comparison and 6 are more than 5% above it; the County Manager is one of the 6.
leadChecks.doesNotEstablish: What the difference consists of, or how to characterize it. The combined wage figure cannot be split into base pay, leave payout, adjustments, or other earnings, and no record supplied characterizes the difference.
leadChecks.recordNeeded: See RN-PAY-09 (County Manager wage and rate difference).
leadChecks.statusReason: The earlier figure and the county's wages-paid figures differ and have not been reconciled; they may measure different things. This does not mean the earlier figure is false.

leadChecks.identityAndTitle: The earlier name reconciliation is supported by two county files: the payroll reports list "Latham, Charlie" and the census lists legal name William Latham, both as Assistant County Manager hired 2020-11-23 at the same base rate as the other two Assistant County Managers. This is a different person from the second employee the census lists under the legal name William Latham (a non-executive position, different hire date, different payroll name). The files carry no employee ID, so the link rests on hire date and position.
leadChecks.finding: OFFICIAL PAYROLL AMOUNTS: FY2024-25 non-OT wages were $177,741.59 plus $342.20 overtime; the FY2025-26 report lists a termination date of 2026-06-30 and $157,431.56 in non-OT wages, with no reason stated. The census lists a current annualized rate of $183,279.12, which equals 1.0300 × the earlier $177,941 figure. The earlier figure is $199.41 above the FY2024-25 wages reported and may have been an annualized rate at an earlier point in time.
leadChecks.doesNotEstablish: The reason employment ended, what the earlier figure measured, or anything about the FY2025-26 amount beyond what was reported.
leadChecks.statusReason: Title, employer, hire date, and pay level are confirmed by official records; the specific $177,941 is not reproduced by any county wages-paid figure and may be a different measurement.

claim.name: Lorin Mock
claim.priorSource: third-party salary aggregator; a local outlet separately reported $213,778

leadChecks.identityAndTitle: Confirmed by official records: payroll and census both list Lorin Mock as Fire Chief, hired 2009-11-04. The census lists the current position's effective date as 2009-11-04, which is consistent with the previously verified 2009 start; the census tenure field is unreliable and is not used.
leadChecks.finding: OFFICIAL PAYROLL AMOUNTS: FY2024-25 non-OT wages were $207,297.33 plus $361.84 overtime; FY2025-26 through September 16, 2026 was $205,317.49 with no overtime. The census lists a current annualized rate of $212,457.63, which equals 1.0300 × the earlier $206,270 figure. The $213,778 figure reported by a local outlet matches none of these county amounts, and what it measured is not known.
leadChecks.doesNotEstablish: Which of the two earlier figures, if either, the outlet derived its number from, or anything about whether additional compensation existed for any other role (see the open Fire Chief question below).
leadChecks.statusReason: The two earlier figures still disagree with each other and neither has been reconciled to a county amount. $206,270 matches the annualized-rate arithmetic; $213,778 has no match.

lorinMockQuestion.question: Do the county's payroll records show any identifiable additional compensation for Lorin Mock serving as Fire Chief while also holding an acting or deputy county-management role?
lorinMockQuestion.answer: The records supplied cannot answer it. The question stays open, and nothing here implies that additional compensation did or did not exist.
whatTheRecordsShow: Both payroll reports and the census list Lorin Mock in one position only: Fire Chief.
No county-manager, deputy-county-manager, or acting title appears for him in any of the three spreadsheets.
Wages are reported as one combined non-OT figure per period.
The reports contain no earnings-code, stipend, acting-pay, or leave-payout field.
whyTheyCannotAnswerIt: A single combined wage figure cannot show whether any component relates to a second role.
Each worker has one position row per report, so a concurrent or temporary assignment would not appear as a separate line.
The census shows only the current position and rate.

The reports cover October 1, 2024 onward. The dates of the reported acting/deputy county-management arrangement are not established in this project's research; if it ended before October 1, 2024 these records do not cover it.
lorinMockQuestion.doesNotEstablish: That he did or did not receive additional compensation. Nothing in these records supports either statement.
lorinMockQuestion.separateFromDisprovenClaim: This is a separate question from the disproven Fire Chief / Fire Marshal claim. The Fire Chief (Lorin Mock) and Fire Marshal (Anthony Roseberry) are different people, and the payroll reports and census list them as two separate employees in two separate positions.
lorinMockQuestion.davidMotesNote: David Motes appears as "Deputy Chief - Administration" in FY2024-25 and "Assistant Fire Chief" in FY2025-26 (census position effective 2026-05-06). No county-manager title appears for him in any of the files.
